description: Reads the existing reversible ordered-tree–Dyck-word encoding, one-step contraction simulations, full soundness/completeness theorem, printed-containment counterexample, and indexed original-token witness guarantees, including a six-bit worked example.

related_resources.reason: Ordered rooted-tree edge contraction, Dyck balanced-word interpretation and the paper’s printed containment definition.
Mutual structural induction, equivalences, and reflexive-transitive closure proofs.

learning_objectives: Explain the distinction between a bijective encoding and a correctness-preserving operation simulation
Trace the first-child/next-sibling representation and both encode/decode round trips
Identify both directions of embeds_iff_dyckEmbeds and why context induction is needed
Reproduce the 001011 contraction example and distinguish the printed containment relation
Explain why original token coordinates and pair identities require further theorems
